---
title: "Q2D: per-unit-length line parameters"
description: "Draw a transmission-line cross section with rectangles and extract its C, G, L and R per unit length."
scgsim-kind: "course"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/course/aedt-q2d"

Q2D computes the capacitance, conductance, inductance and resistance per unit
length of a transmission line from its 2D cross section. You draw the cross
section as rectangles; Q2D does not slice a GDS file or a 3D model.

This example is a CPW: 10 µm signal, 10 µm gaps, 40 µm ground strips,
0.2 µm Nb on a 200 µm-wide, 500 µm-thick silicon substrate. It needs the
`aedt` extra; see [Install SCGSim](installation.qmd).

## Set up and prepare the run

```python
from pathlib import Path
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk.materials import get_material_records
from scgsim.aedt import (
    MatrixRunControl, PdkMaterial, Q2dConductorSpec,
    Q2dRectangleSpec, Q2dSpec, prepare_handoff,
)

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
records = get_material_records()
materials = {
    name: PdkMaterial(name, records[name]["material_kind"],
                      records[name]["is_superconducting"],
                      records[name]["aedt_library_name"])
    for name in ("vacuum", "Si", "Nb")
}
rectangles = (
    Q2dRectangleSpec("Substrate", (-100.0, -500.0), (200.0, 500.0), "Si"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("Signal", (-5.0, 0.0), (10.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("GroundLeft", (-55.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("GroundRight", (15.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
)
conductors = (
    Q2dConductorSpec("Signal", "SignalLine", ("Signal",), 0.2),
    Q2dConductorSpec("Ground", "ReferenceGround", ("GroundLeft", "GroundRight"), 0.2),
)
spec = Q2dSpec(
    project_name="cpw_q2d", design_name="CpwFiniteGroundQ2d",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    rectangles=rectangles, conductors=conductors,
    run_control=MatrixRunControl("Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3),
    region_padding_um=(100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 100.0),
)
print(spec.to_payload())
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/cpw-q2d"))
print(handoff.run_dir)
```

- `Q2dRectangleSpec(name, lower_left_um, size_um, material)` is one
  rectangle. Check each position and size against the gaps you intend;
  `spec.to_payload()` prints the full specification.
- `Q2dConductorSpec(name, kind, rectangles, thickness_um)` groups rectangles
  into a conductor. You need exactly one `ReferenceGround` and at least one
  `SignalLine`. Every metal rectangle must belong to exactly one conductor.
- Do not draw vacuum; it comes from the region padding.
- `region_padding_um` has four values in the order **(-X, +X, -Y, +Y)**. This
  differs from the six-value order used by HFSS and Q3D.

To build the model in AEDT without solving, pass `run_control=None`; see
[Q2D model-only preparation](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-native-model-only-preparation).

## Run and read the result

[Run the directory](execute.qmd), then [load it](returned-results.qmd):

```python
from scgsim.aedt import resolve_results

result = resolve_results(".artifacts/cpw-q2d")
blocks = result.physics_results()
```

Q2D writes one file, `results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv`, with C, G, L and R
blocks in conductor order, per unit length, at the extraction frequency.

Per-unit-length capacitance is not the same as the total capacitance of a
finite structure. For that, use [Q3D](aedt-q3d.qmd) or
[Palace Electrostatic](palace-electrostatic.qmd).

See the [Q2D export reference](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-native-combined-matrix-export)
for the file format, and
[matrix convergence records](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations)
for the adaptive history.
